defects.summary: ROUND 5 INTRODUCED: `--check-current --only <source> --ref <another commit>` produces a FALSE shrink refusal naming the PRIMARY's bundles, prints no command, and suppresses a remediation the generator accepts at exit 0. Round 4's generator printed that command.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:2266 `primary_moves = (kind == "primary" or primary_drifted or ref != existing.get("ref"))` — the clause added by 2adbb27 — feeds :2280 `_movable_bundles(...)`, so a SCOPED run whose `--ref` differs from the lock's pin marks the primary's bundles movable. But `working` on a `--only <source>` run is check_current's reading of that source ALONE (main: `_select_sources` returns include_primary False, so the primary's tree is never read), so `after` has no primary-bundle keys while `before` does — and repin_shrink_blocker reports the primary's bundle as emptied.

MEASURED (scratchpad/v7/onlyref.py, onlyref2.py). Lock: primary `adam` + federated source `cms-platform`; primary advanced by one commit (HEAD != pinned ref); source content drifted.
  `--check-current --only <src>`            -> exit 1, PRINTS `--repin --ref <lock ref> --repin-source '<src>@' ...`; RAN -> exit 0.
  `--check-current --only <src> --ref HEAD` -> exit 1, ZERO commands, headline: "No --repin-source command is printed for it because this generator would refuse one: the re-pin would leave bundle(s) adam with no skills at all — a bundle directory stopped existing at the commit this would pin: a rename, a deleted plugin, a layout change."
  The command it declined to print, run anyway: `--repin --ref <HEAD> --repin-source '<src>@' --repo <primary> -o <lock>` -> exit 0 | "Wrote ...: 2 skills"; skills before == skills after (['adam/alpha','cms-platform/deploy']); registry, bundles and the sources array unchanged.
  Same shape against the ROUND 4 generator (git show 21a95e0) -> exit 1 and the command IS printed. So this is a regression, not a pre-existing hole.

Both halves of round 4's D2 are back: (a) the report suppresses a repair the apply path accepts, and (b) the sentence asserts something a reader can check and find false — `bundles` is ["adam"], `plugins/adam/skills/` exists at every commit involved, and no `--repin` can make that sentence true.

BLAST RADIUS, measured by re-running the round-5 matrix property over the one invocation form it omits (scratchpad/v7/extend.py, all 21 `_MATRIX_SHAPES` x `--check-current --only <each registry> --ref HEAD`): 4 cells refuse on a shrink; 2 are legitimate (`a source bundle lost every skill`), 2 are this false refusal — `both moved` and `the primary bundle is gone at HEAD and a source drifted`, both naming `adam`.

WHY THE MATRIX MISSES IT: `_report_invocations` (test:7418) emits `--check-current --only <r>` and `--check-current --ref HEAD` as separate cells and never the product. The two flags are independently legal (main's only guards are `--only` requires `--check-current`, and `--only` excludes `--check`/`--check-format`), and this defect lives exactly in their intersection.

defects.summary: THE CLASS IS STILL OPEN on `--source-repo`: every command every report path prints omits it, so on any machine where a federated source's checkout is not the default sibling `../<repo-name>`, the printed line exits 1. `_addressing` carries `--repo` and `-o` and stops there.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:2101 `_addressing(output, repo)` restates only `--repo` and `-o`; `remediation`'s three other branches add nothing. main builds `overrides = dict(parse_source_repo(spec) for spec in args.source_repo or [])` and uses it on every path, but `remediation` is never given it and no printed line mentions it. `--source-repo` is deliberately NOT in --repin's `overriding` error list precisely because "a federated re-pin needs [it] on a machine whose siblings are not at the default path" (main's own comment), so this is a supported input, not an exotic one.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v7/srcrepo.py and srcrepo2.py. Lock: primary at `<tmp>/registry`, source registry `file://<tmp>/deep/cms-platform` (sibling lookup resolves to `<tmp>/cms-platform`, which does not exist), generated with `--source-repo 'cms-platform=<tmp>/deep/cms-platform'`. Every run below repeats that flag; every printed line drops it:
  * `--check` (lock hand-made stale): printed `... --registry <uri> --ref <sha> --bundles adam --source 'cms-platform=<uri>@<sha>:skills' --repo <primary> -o <lock>`; RAN VERBATIM -> exit 1 | "ERROR: file://.../deep/cms-platform: no checkout at <tmp>/cms-platform — clone it there, or point at it with --source-repo 'cms-platform=<path>'".
  * `--check-current` unscoped, primary block: printed `--repin --repo <primary> -o <lock>`; RAN -> exit 1, same ERROR (a bare --repin re-plans the whole document, sources included).
  * `--check-current` unscoped, source block: printed `--repin --repin-source '<uri>@' --repo <primary> -o <lock>`; RAN -> exit 1, same ERROR.
  * `--check-current --only <src>`: printed `--repin --ref <sha> --repin-source '<uri>@' --repo <primary> -o <lock>`; RAN -> exit 1, same ERROR.

So the round's central assertion — "every printed `python3 ...` line is RUN VERBATIM ... must exit 0" — holds only for the fixture layout. `_report_invocations` never passes `--source-repo` and every `_MATRIX_SHAPES` builder puts its source at the default sibling, so this column of the product does not exist. `_addressing`'s docstring ("The flags a printed command needs to reach the same lock and clone") names the property it does not deliver: `--source-repo` is precisely "where this source's clone is".

defects.summary: `report_digest_format`'s docstring and `--check-format`'s argparse help both assert a read-set that 36dfb87 made false: the flag now reads `registry`, `bundles`, `sources` and `--repo`.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:1601 still says "Reads `skills`, and `ref` only to name it in the remediation command below — no `registry`, no `sources`, and no git", and :2523-2526 still says `--repo` "is accepted ... but is never READ here, so the verdict cannot depend on which clone, or no clone, is at hand." Round 5 changed the signature to `report_digest_format(document, output, repo)` and routed it through `remediation("format", ...)`, which consults repin_inherit_blocker (registry, bundles, sources), repin_primary_blocker, repin_unproven_sources_blocker and repin_plan_blocker, and calls `_addressing(output, repo)`.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v7/fmtdoc.py, on a lock with bare (unlabelled) digests:
  * `registry` removed -> `FAILED: 1 of 1 digests ... No re-pin command is printed for it because this generator would refuse one: ...: 'registry' is missing or unusable (None) ...` (registry read)
  * `"sources": {}` -> reason "...will not silently drop a federated source list it cannot read..." (sources read)
  * same lock, `--check-format -o <lock>` vs `--check-format -o <lock> --repo <primary>` print DIFFERENT lines — the second adds `--repo <primary>` (repo read).
No git call is made, so that half of the sentence survives; the rest does not. The help text is a cross-repo contract (the fleet bumper's per-consumer pre-clone call), which is why the stale half matters beyond tidiness.

defects.summary: `test_no_report_path_writes_a_command_of_its_own` is a four-substring blacklist, so a NAMED report path can still build and print a complete remediation by using the module-level `_SCRIPT`. The gate stays green.
defects.evidence:
test_generate_skills_lock.py:3733 asserts only that no non-docstring string constant in report_drift / report_digest_format / main contains "python3", "generate_skills_lock", "--repin-source '" or "--source '". `_SCRIPT` is an ast.Name, not a Constant, and the remaining literals of a self-built line (" --repin --ref ", "@") match nothing.

MEASURED: patched report_drift to print, right after its own `FAILED: ... {invite}` line, `f"  {_SCRIPT} --repin --ref {ref} --repin-source " + chr(39) + str(registry) + "@" + chr(39)`. `python3 -m pytest scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py -k test_no_report_path_writes_a_command_of_its_own` -> "1 passed". Generator restored; `git status --short` clean.

This is a different hole from the one stillOpen names (a NEW top-level report path outside `_REPORT_PATHS`): this one is inside the three functions the gate does scan. The docstring's claim — "no function that PRINTS a verdict may contain a string that looks like a command" — is what the test cannot enforce. A check on the call graph (does this function reference `_SCRIPT`, or print a value it did not get from `remediation`) would; a substring list will not.

defects.summary: `remediation`'s docstring claims the blockers are composed "in the order the apply path meets them, so the sentence quoted is the sentence the flag says" — but plan and source are swapped relative to main, so a lock tripping both quotes the wrong refusal.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:2182 makes the claim. remediation composes inherit -> primary -> unproven -> **plan** -> **source** -> shrink (:2255-2264). main's apply path meets inherit (`_repin_inherit_guard`) -> primary+unproven (`_repin_primary_guard`) -> **source** (`_apply_repin_sources`) -> **plan** (`build_lock` -> `plan_sources`) -> shrink.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v7/order.py — a 9-source lock (over MAX_SOURCES) whose 9th entry repeats source[0]'s registry under a different bundle, asked about that registry:
  REPORT (`gsl.remediation("source", ...)`): "'sources' lists 9 entries; at most 8 are allowed ..."
  APPLY  (`--repin --repin-source '<that registry>@'`): exit 1 | "ERROR: --repin-source <reg>: this lock federates that registry twice ..."
No command is printed either way, so nothing is recommended that would be refused; the cost is a reader told to fix the wrong field first, and a docstring sentence that is checkable and false. `test_the_report_and_the_refusal_give_the_same_reason` does not cover the pair because it rebuilds the apply command by hand for shapes that trip only one blocker.
